questions: Did s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.3 and 1.9 per run? Report the count per track and the off-track count.
Did the oval finish rate hold at 16/20 or better, and did oval steering_oscillation stay under about 0.35? A lighter robot may make the oval jittery.
Did completion_time or progress change on any track, which would show that the lower mass affected speed or slip?
If line-loss is still at 1.3 or more on s-bend with the controller unchanged, do you agree that the remaining gap is the controller's response and that geometry has no further lever to test?
feedback_request.suggested_changes_to_test: If mass 0.5 lowers s-bend line-loss to 1.0 or below with the oval holding, keep it and let the Integrator tune controller weights or kp. If the oval drops below about 14/20 or oscillation exceeds about 0.35 with low max_error, return mass to 0.7 kg. Do not change wheel_track, span, footprint or y in this step.

intent: Single-variable test of body inertia: keep the iteration 6 geometry (best score 372.2) and reduce mass from 0.7 to 0.5 kg to lower yaw inertia on the sharp bends. The Integrator should keep the controller unchanged so the race isolates mass. Success means s-bend line-loss falls toward 1.0 or below and max_error stays under 0.06 m, with the oval finish rate holding at 16/20 or better.
learning: Iterations 4 to 6 showed that forward position helped the oval and that narrowing wheel_track to 0.09 m gave only small gains on the sharp tracks (s-bend line-loss 1.4 to 1.3). Span and footprint changes both hurt. The mass test is the last untested body lever. A flat result would indicate that geometry is exhausted and the Integrator should focus on controller weights, kp and line-loss mode.
rationale: Iteration 6 (wheel_track 0.09 m, otherwise iteration 5) is the new best at 372.2. The oval held at 17/20 finishes with max_error 0.0435 m and steering_oscillation 0.30, below the 0.35 threshold. The sharp tracks did not improve: s-bend line-loss stayed at 1.3 per run with max_error 0.064 m and 0/20 finishes, and slalom stayed at 1.9 with 0/20. The narrowing trend from 0.11 to 0.09 m gave small gains and then flattened. Both the Integrator's rule (b) and their rule (c) apply. Narrowing is now at its floor (0.09 m, do not go narrower), and the remaining gap is more likely the controller's response on sharp bends. Span, footprint, forward position and wheel_radius have each been tested or ruled out (iterations 2, 3, 4 and the 1.8 s oval finish). Mass is the one body-side lever not yet tested cleanly. Iteration 0 to 1 changed mass 0.8 to 0.7 together with wheel_track and sensors, so its effect was confounded. Yaw inertia is mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, so lowering mass lowers the inertia the robot must overcome to turn on sharp bends. I therefore keep the best-known geometry (wheel_track 0.09, y 0.07, span ±0.03 m at 0.015 m spacing, footprint 0.012 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body unchanged) and change only mass from 0.7 to 0.5 kg. The Integrator's controller stays unchanged, so the race isolates mass. Expected result: s-bend line-loss falls from 1.3 toward 1.0 or below and slalom line-loss moves from 1.9 down. The oval should hold at 16/20 or better. If mass alone does not move line-loss on the sharp tracks, the next lever is the controller, not geometry.
